words.gloss: sirā (vessel, here blood-carrying vessel; vein, probable); division

hindi: अब इसलिए हम शरीर सम्बन्धी सिराओं यानी वाहिनियों के विभाग की व्याख्या करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall explain the bodily division of the sirās (vessels).
notes: sirā = vessel; in this tradition it covers the veins and other blood-carrying vessels (probable); the Sanskrit term is kept. 'śārīra' (bodily) is taken with vibhāga.

words.gloss: ojas (vital essence; doctrinal term, no modern equivalent)

hindi: हृदय से बँधी हुई दस मूलसिराएँ सब अंगों और प्रत्यंगों तक ओज यानी जीवन-सार को ले जाती हैं।
english: Ten root-sirās (mūlasirā), bound to the heart (hṛdaya), carry ojas (vital essence) to all the limbs (aṅga) and sub-limbs (pratyaṅga).

text_flags.why: possible: the long ā between -nyā- and -ojo- looks like a stray vowel; -āni + ojaḥ gives -āny ojo

notes: 'mūlasirā' stands for mūlasirāḥ before h- (āḥ before a voiced sound drops its visarga: regular, no flag). ojas is a doctrinal term (vital essence) with no modern equivalent; it is kept. The two accusatives with nayanti: ojas is what is carried, the limbs and sub-limbs where it is carried to.

hindi: क्योंकि शरीर की चेष्टाएँ उनसे बँधी हैं।
english: For the activities (ceṣṭā) of the body are bound to those.
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue line 2 (card 2); 'tat' is understood to refer to the ten root-sirās there. 'tatpratibaddhā' for tatpratibaddhāḥ before h-: regular sandhi.

words.gloss: tree; leaf; sevanī (seam, thread; sense uncertain); spreading; like
being dispersed (printed form; possibly vibhajyamānāḥ, being divided)
words.gram: pass. part. vi-√dham, f. nom. pl.

hindi: वे तो दो अङ्गुल, अङ्गुल, आधा अङ्गुल, यव और आधा यव जाकर, वृक्ष के पत्ते की सेवनी जिसका अर्थ अनिश्चित है उसके फैलाव की तरह बिखरती हुई सात सौ हो जाती हैं।
english: But those, having gone two aṅgulas, an aṅgula, half an aṅgula, a yava (barley-grain) and half a yava, being dispersed like the spreading of the sevanī (sense uncertain) of a tree's leaf, become seven hundred.

text_flags.why: possible: 'vidhamyamāna' (being blown apart) is a real word but 'vibhajyamāna' (being divided) fits a count of branches; bha/dha and ja/ma are easily confused in print

notes: 'tāḥ' = the sirās (understood; the branches of the ten root-sirās of line 2 (card 2)). aṅgula = finger-breadth, yava = barley-grain, both measures; not converted. The sevanī-pratāna simile is not firm: sevanī is 'seam, stitching' elsewhere and the exact picture (leaf veins?) is not stated, so it is kept as printed with the sense marked uncertain. The measures are read as successive stages of the branching; the wording does not say whether length or thickness. Printed 'vidhamyamānāḥ' (dispersed) may be a misreading of vibhajyamānāḥ (divided): bha/dha and ja/ma are close in print; both senses suit 'branching out', so the printed word is kept and flagged as possible. Orthography: -rdd- written -rd- in w.
lines_deva: तास्तु द्व्यंगुलमंगुलमर्द्धंगुलं यवं यवार्द्धं च गत्वा द्रुमपत्रसेवनीप्रतानवद्विधम्यमानाः सप्त शतानि भवंति
lines_iast: tāstu dvyaṃgulamaṃgulamarddhaṃgulaṃ yavaṃ yavārddhaṃ ca gatvā drumapatrasevanīpratānavadvidhamyamānāḥ sapta śatāni bhavaṃti

words.gloss: four; hundred (a set of four hundred)
in the limbs (śākhā, literally branches; the arms and legs, standard)

hindi: उनमें चार सौ शाखाओं यानी हाथ-पैरों में हैं।
english: Of them, four hundred are in the limbs (śākhā).
notes: Copula understood. śākhā = branch; in this body-division the four limbs (arms and legs), standard. GROUPING: appears to continue line 4 (card 4) (the seven hundred).

hindi: उनमें सोलह बेधने योग्य नहीं हैं।
english: Among those, sixteen are not to be pierced.
notes: Copula understood. 'tatra' is read as 'among those' (the four hundred of line 5 (card 5)). vyadh = pierce; in practice venepuncture or bloodletting is meant (probable), but the literal 'pierced' is kept.

hindi: अन्तराधि यानी धड़ में एक सौ छत्तीस।
english: One hundred and thirty-six in the antarādhi (trunk, probable).
notes: 'ṣaṭtriṃśaṃ śatam' is read as a hundred with thirty-six added = 136. antarādhi = the trunk, the part between the limbs and the head: probable. Copula understood. Arithmetic aside: 400 (line 5 (card 5)) + 136 + 164 (line 9 (card 9)) = 700 (line 4 (card 4)). GROUPING: appears to continue line 5 (card 5).

hindi: उनमें बाईस।
english: Among those, twenty-two.

text_flags.why: possible, and likely: tatra (as in u6 and u9) gives the number of sirās not to be pierced within the trunk's 136, so 22 does not clash with 136. The trunk lists that name sirās to be guarded add up to 8 (u13) + 2 (u14) + 4 (u16) + 4 (u18) + 14 (u23) = 32, which is dvātriṃśat; dvāviṃśat and dvātriṃśat differ by one letter. Not applied; the printed 22 is translated

notes: Number translated as printed, not corrected. tatra is read as in line 6 (card 6) (sixteen not to be pierced) and line 9 (card 9) (fifty): 'among those (the 136 of the trunk)', a subset of sirās not to be pierced; this is an inference from the parallel wording, not stated. 22 therefore does not conflict with the 136, but the guarded sirās named in lines 13-23 (card 12/21) add up to 32 (8 + 2 + 4 + 4 + 14), so the printed dvāviṃśat is probably a misreading of dvātriṃśat; flagged as possible, not applied. Copula understood. GROUPING: appears to continue line 7 (card 7).

words.gloss: thigh, leg (sakthi); printed form, locative sg. would be sakthni
jāladharā (name of a vessel, apparently; literally net-bearing; sense uncertain)

hindi: एक सौ चौंसठ ऊपर; उनमें भी पचास। उनमें प्रत्येक सक्थि यानी जाँघ में सौ; उनमें जालधरा को न बेधे।
english: One hundred and sixty-four above; among those also, fifty. Of them, a hundred in each thigh (sakthi). Among those, one should not pierce the jāladharā,

text_flags.why: possible: the locative singular of sakthi is sakthni (or sakthini); printed 'sakthi' looks like a lost -n-

notes: [02.06.9] 'catuḥṣaṣṭyadhikaṃ śatam' = a hundred with sixty-four in excess = 164. 'ūrdhvam' = above (the upper part of the body); it is not further defined in the line. What the fifty are is not stated. Copula understood. 400 + 136 + 164 = 700 as in line 4 (card 4). Arithmetic check (not stated in the text): the sirās named for guarding in the upper part, lines 26-38 (card 24/36), give 16 + 2 + 4 + 3 + 6 + 7 + 4 + 8 = 50, which suggests the fifty are the ones not to be pierced, as in lines 6 and 8 (card 6/8); the ear total of 4 in line 36 (card 34) is itself an inference. [02.06.10] The printed '|' after śataṃ is a punctuation mark inside the unit; it ends the first clause. 'sakthi' is the thigh or leg; the four limbs would give 4 x 100 = 400 (line 5 (card 5)), but the line names only sakthi, so 'thigh' is kept as printed and not widened. Printed 'sakthi' is not the usual locative (sakthni): possible slip, flagged. jāladharā: taken as a name of a kind of sirā (apparently, from the context 'not to be pierced'); the literal sense 'net-bearing' is uncertain and nothing is added. GROUPING: appears to continue in line 11 (card 10), which supplies further objects of 'na vidhyet'.

hindi: और आड़ी तथा भीतर जाने वाली।
english: and (ones) going across and within.
notes: GROUPING: appears to complete line 10 (card 9): 'tiras ca abhyantaragāḥ' are further objects of 'na vidhyet' (not translated as a full sentence here because the verb belongs to line 10 (card 9)). tiras is taken as an adverb with -gāḥ; 'across' may also mean 'oblique'.

words.gloss: in the śroṇi (hip region, pelvis; standard)
anus (guda; standard); penis (meḍhra; standard); seat, support

hindi: बत्तीस श्रोणि यानी कटि-प्रदेश में, जिनका आश्रय गुद यानी मलद्वार और मेढ्र यानी शिश्न है।
english: Thirty-two in the śroṇi (hip region), having the guda (anus) and meḍhra (penis) as their seat.
notes: Copula understood. Printed meḍhra with an anusvara (meṃḍhra), a variant spelling of meḍhra; normalised in w. 'āśraya' = seat, support; the line does not say more about how they rest.

words.gloss: in the two kaṭīkataruṇas (name of a marma)
pārśvasandhi (name of a marma); name, called

hindi: उनमें दो-दो दोनों वंक्षणों यानी जाँघ के मूल में और दोनों कटीकतरुणों में, इस प्रकार आठ; अनुमानित पाठ पर शस्त्र से रक्षा करे। सोलह दोनों पार्श्वों यानी बगलों में; उन दोनों में एक-एक ऊपर जाने वाली, पार्श्वसन्धि नाम वाली।
english: Of them, two each in the two groins (vaṅkṣaṇa) and in the two kaṭīkataruṇas, thus eight; on a conjectural reading, one should guard (them) from the knife (śastra). Sixteen in the two sides (pārśva); of those two, one each going upward, named pārśvasandhi.

text_flags.why: possible: 'śakhato' is not a word; śastrataḥ (from the knife) with rakṣet fits the sense of lines 26 and 38 (card 24/36); kha/stra confusion

notes: [02.06.13] Printed 'śakhato' is not a word. On a conjectural reading it is śastrataḥ (from the knife), as in lines 26 and 38 (card 24/36) where the same kind of list ends 'śastreṇa na spṛśet' / 'śastreṇa pariharet'; kha for stra is a plausible misreading. The conjecture is hedged in both translations. 'kaṭīkataruṇa' is a marma name in this tradition (probable); marma = vital spot (doctrinal term). 'aṣṭau' = 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 over the groins and the kaṭīkataruṇas. [02.06.14] Elliptical: the accusatives suggest that a verb such as rakṣet (line 13 (card 12)) is understood; none is supplied. 'tayoḥ' = of the two sides. pārśvasandhi is a marma name in this tradition (probable). GROUPING: appears to continue line 13 (card 12).
lines_deva: तासां द्वे द्वे वंक्षणयोः कटीकतरुणयोश्चेत्यष्टौशखतो रक्षेत्
lines_iast: tāsāṃ dve dve vaṃkṣaṇayoḥ kaṭīkataruṇayoścetyaṣṭauśakhato rakṣet

hindi: पीठ में चौबीस।
english: Twenty-four in the back (pṛṣṭha).
notes: Copula understood.

hindi: उनमें पृष्ठवंश यानी रीढ़ के दोनों ओर दो-दो ऊपर जाने वाली; वे चार हैं।
english: Of them, on both sides of the pṛṣṭhavaṃśa (spine), two and two going upward; those are four.
notes: Copula understood in the last clause. GROUPING: appears to continue line 15 (card 13).
lines_deva: तासां पृष्ठवंशमुभयतो द्वे द्वे ऊर्ध्वगामिन्यौ ताश्चतस्रः
lines_iast: tāsāṃ pṛṣṭhavaṃśamubhayato dve dve ūrdhvagāminyau tāścatasraḥ

hindi: पेट में चौबीस।
english: Twenty-four in the belly (udara).
notes: Copula understood.

hindi: उनमें मेढ्र यानी शिश्न के ऊपर, रोमराजी यानी रोमों की रेखा के दोनों ओर, दो-दो; वे भी चार हैं।
english: Of them, above the meḍhra (penis), on both sides of the romarājī (line of body hair), two and two; those also are four.

text_flags.why: near certain: 'omarājī' is not a word; the ra of romarājī (line of body hair) has dropped out in print

notes: Printed 'upariomarājīm': the ra of romarājī is lost (the Devanagari shows a bare vowel sign); romarājī, the line of body hair, is a known word; near certain. 'tā api' for tāḥ api: regular sandhi. Printed meṃḍhra = meḍhra. GROUPING: appears to continue line 17 (card 15).
lines_deva: तासां मेंढ्रस्योपरिोमराजीमुभयतो द्वे द्वे ताअपि चतस्रः
lines_iast: tāsāṃ meṃḍhrasyopariomarājīmubhayato dve dve tāapi catasraḥ

hindi: वक्ष यानी छाती में चालीस।
english: Forty in the chest (vakṣas).
notes: Copula understood.

hindi: उनमें दो हृदय में।
english: Of them, two in the heart (hṛdaya).
notes: Copula understood. GROUPING: appears to continue line 19 (card 17) (the chest).

words.gloss: stanamūla (breast-root, a named place); stanarohita (a named place; sense of rohita uncertain)

hindi: और दो-दो स्तनमूलों और स्तनरोहितों में।
english: And two and two in the stanamūlas and the stanarohitas.
notes: Copula understood. stanamūla and stanarohita are names of marmas in this tradition (probable); the line does not say so, so they are kept as names. GROUPING: appears to continue line 20 (card 18). Arithmetic check (not stated): the chest sirās to be guarded come to 14 (line 23 (card 21)) only if 'dve dve' means two on each side in each of the stanamūla and stanarohita: 2 (heart) + 4 + 4 + 4 (apastambha, apalāpa) = 14. The translation keeps the plural place names and does not decide this.

words.gloss: apastambha (a named place; name of a marma in this tradition, probable)
apalāpa (a named place; on a conjectural reading)

hindi: एक-एक अपस्तम्भों और अपलापों में, अनुमानित पाठ पर; इस प्रकार।
english: One each in the apastambhas and the apalāpas (on a conjectural reading), thus.

text_flags.why: possible: 'ālāpa' (talk) is not a body place; apalāpa (a known name beside apastambha) fits with the p lost

notes: Printed 'ālāpa' (talk) does not suit a list of body places; apalāpa, a name in the same series (probable), with the p lost, fits. The conjecture is hedged in both translations. The avagraha after -ā (ekaikā'pastaṃbhā-) is a print habit (ā + a). Copula understood. GROUPING: appears to continue line 21 (card 19).

hindi: वे चौदह हैं।
english: Those are fourteen.
notes: Copula understood. 'tāḥ' = those counted in lines 20-22 (card 18/20) (appears). GROUPING: appears to complete lines 19-22 (card 17/20) (the chest total of forty is given in line 19 (card 17); fourteen is a part). Arithmetic: 14 = 2 (heart) + 4 (stanamūlas) + 4 (stanarohitas) + 4 (apastambhas and apalāpas) if 'dve dve' in line 21 (card 19) gives two on each side; this is an inference, the print gives only the total.

hindi: ग्रीवा यानी गर्दन में चौबीस।
english: Twenty-four in the neck (grīvā).
notes: Copula understood.

words.gloss: marma (vital spot; doctrinal term); name, called

hindi: उनमें चार और आठ मर्म यानी जीवन-स्थल नाम वाली हैं।
english: Of them, four and eight are named marma (vital spot).
notes: Copula understood. marma is a doctrinal term (vital spot) and is kept. GROUPING: appears to continue line 24 (card 22).

words.gloss: in the two kṛkāṭikās (name of a marma, at the junction of head and neck behind; probable)
in the two vidhuras (name of a marma, behind the ear; probable)

hindi: दो दोनों कृकाटिकाओं में और दो दोनों विधुरों में, इस प्रकार सोलह; शस्त्र से न छुए।
english: Two in the two kṛkāṭikās and two in the two vidhuras, thus sixteen; one should not touch (them) with the knife (śastra).
notes: Both names are marma names in this tradition (probable). 'sixteen' = 4 + 8 of line 25 (card 23) plus these 2 + 2. Printed 'dvevidhurayoriti' = dve vidhurayoḥ iti. GROUPING: appears to complete line 25 (card 23).
lines_deva: द्वे कृकाटिकयोर्द्वेविधुरयोरिति षोडश शस्त्रेण न स्पृशेत्
lines_iast: dve kṛkāṭikayordvevidhurayoriti ṣoḍaśa śastreṇa na spṛśet

hindi: दोनों हनु यानी जबड़ों में सोलह; उनमें दो सन्धि से सम्बद्ध।
english: In the two jaws (hanu), sixteen; of them, two connected with the joint (sandhi).
notes: Copula understood. Which joint is not stated (the jaw joint is the natural but unstated reading).

hindi: जिह्वा यानी जीभ में सोलह।
english: Sixteen in the tongue (jihvā).
notes: Printed 'jivhā' is a letter reversal of jihvā (recorded once; normalised in w). Copula understood.

words.gloss: speech; setting in motion, bringing about

hindi: उनके नीचे दो रस यानी स्वाद का बोध करने वाली और दो वाणी को प्रवृत्त करने वाली; वे चार हैं।
english: Below them, two perceiving taste (rasa) and two setting speech in motion; those are four.
notes: 'tāsām adhaḥ' is read as 'below them'; 'of them, underneath' is the alternative. Copula understood in the last clause. GROUPING: appears to continue line 28 (card 26) (the tongue).

hindi: नासा यानी नाक में चौबीस।
english: Twenty-four in the nose (nāsā).
notes: Copula understood.

hindi: उनमें दो गन्ध का बोध करने वाली, और उन्हीं में से एक तालु में; इस प्रकार तीन।
english: Of them, two perceiving smell (gandha); and of those very ones, one in the palate (tālu); thus three.
notes: Elliptical: 'ekām' is accusative with no verb; none is supplied. 'tāsām eva' = of those very ones (the 24 of the nose, appears). GROUPING: appears to continue line 30 (card 28).
lines_deva: तासां द्वे गंधवेदिन्यौ तासामेव च तालुन्येकामिति तिस्रः
lines_iast: tāsāṃ dve gaṃdhavedinyau tāsāmeva ca tālunyekāmiti tisraḥ

hindi: दोनों नेत्रों में छप्पन।
english: Fifty-six in the two eyes (netra).
notes: Copula understood. Printed 'ṣaṭpaṃcāśannetrayoḥ' = ṣaṭpañcāśat netrayoḥ (t before n becomes n: regular).

words.gloss: in the two apāṅgas (outer corners of the eye; standard)

hindi: उन दोनों में उन्मेष और निमेष की क्रियाएँ: दो, दो; और दो दोनों अपाङ्गों में; इस प्रकार छह।
english: Of those two, the two actions of opening (unmeṣa) and closing (nimeṣa): two, two; and two in the two apāṅgas (outer corners of the eye); thus six.
notes: Elliptical, and the distribution is not firm: 'unmeṣanimeṣakriye dve dve' is read as two for the action of opening and two for the action of closing (2 + 2), with 2 more in the apāṅgas, thus six; the dual 'kriye' could also qualify the first 'dve'. apāṅga is also a marma name in this tradition (probable). GROUPING: appears to continue line 32 (card 30).
lines_deva: तयोरुन्मेषनिमेषक्रिये द्वे द्वे द्वे चापांगयोरिति षट्
lines_iast: tayorunmeṣanimeṣakriye dve dve dve cāpāṃgayoriti ṣaṭ

hindi: नासा और नेत्रों तक गई हुई वे तो ललाट में साठ हैं।
english: Those that go to the nose and eyes, however, are sixty in the forehead (lalāṭa).
notes: Copula understood. The line does not say whether the sixty are additional to the 24 of the nose and 56 of the eyes; no relation is stated or assumed. GROUPING: appears to continue line 33 (card 31). Arithmetic check: neck 24 + jaws 16 + tongue 16 + nose 24 + eyes 56 + ears 16 + head 12 = 164 (line 9 (card 9)), so the sixty in the forehead are not additional to the 24 of the nose and 56 of the eyes; they appear to be sirās going to the nose and eyes that lie in the forehead.

in the two āvartas (whorl; a named place, name of a marma in this tradition, probable)
in the sthapanī (a named place, name of a marma in this tradition, probable)

english: Of them, four going along to the keśānta (end of the hair, probably the hair-line); two in the two āvartas; and one in the sthapanī; thus seven.

text_flags.why: possible: keśānta + anugatāḥ joins as keśāntānugatāḥ (long ā); the printed short -a- may be a lost length mark or a lost anusvara (keśāntam anugatāḥ)

lines_deva: तासां केशांतनुगताश्चतस्रो द्वे आवर्तयोरेका च स्थपन्यामिति सप्त
lines_iast: tāsāṃ keśāṃtanugatāścatasro dve āvartayorekā ca sthapanyāmiti sapta

hindi: दोनों कर्णों में सोलह; उनमें दो शब्द को वहन करने वाली; वही दोनों शंखों यानी कनपटियों में भी; उनमें दो शंख की सन्धि तक गई हुई।
english: In the two ears (karṇa), sixteen; of them, two carrying sound (śabda); those very two also in the two śaṅkhas (temples); of them, two gone to the joint (sandhi) of the temple.
notes: Printed 'evaca' joins eva and ca (spacing slip, no flag). The second and third clauses are elliptical; copula understood. The relation of 'those very two' to the two in the temples is as the Sanskrit states it and is not explained further. śaṅkha = temple of the head (the same word means conch); standard here. GROUPING: appears to continue line 35 (card 33). 'te eva' = those very two (the sound-carriers), not two additional ones: this agrees with the arithmetic of line 9 (card 9) (fifty guarded in the upper part needs 4 for the ears: 2 sound-carriers + 2 at the temple joint). Inference, not stated.
lines_deva: कर्णयोः षोडश तासां शब्दवाहिन्यौ द्वे ते एवच शंखयोः तासां शंखसंधिगते द्वे
lines_iast: karṇayoḥ ṣoḍaśa tāsāṃ śabdavāhinyau dve te evaca śaṃkhayoḥ tāsāṃ śaṃkhasaṃdhigate dve

hindi: सिर में बारह।
english: Twelve in the head (mūrdhan).
notes: Printed 'mūrddhani' (-rdd-) normalised to mūrdhani in w. Copula understood.

words.gloss: in the two utkṣepas (a named place on the head, name of a marma in this tradition, probable)
in the sīmantas (a named place; literally parting; name of marmas in this tradition, probable)
in the adhipati (a named place, name of a marma in this tradition, probable)

hindi: उनमें दो दोनों उत्क्षेपों में, एक-एक सीमन्तों में, एक अधिपति में; इस प्रकार आठ; शस्त्र से परिहार करे।
english: Of them, two in the two utkṣepas; one each in the sīmantas; one in the adhipati; thus eight: one should avoid (them) with the knife (śastra).
notes: The accusatives ekaikām and ekām have no governing verb in the clause; none is supplied. The numbers fit 2 + 5 + 1 = 8 only if there are five sīmantas, which the line does not state. GROUPING: appears to continue line 37 (card 35) (the head).

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर, इसी प्रकार छोटी, टेढ़ी, मिली हुई, गुँथी हुई और जोड़ों में, शस्त्र-कर्म के योग्य नहीं हैं।
english: Likewise (on a conjectural reading of the first word), the small, crooked, intermingled and knotted ones, and those in the joints, are not to be dealt with by the knife (śastra).

text_flags.why: possible: 'na tathā' would clash with the following negative aśastrakṛtyāḥ (double negative); 'tathā' (likewise) opens a further class naturally; the na may be a stray stroke

notes: Printed 'natathā': read na + tathā it would give a double negative with aśastrakṛtyāḥ; the stray na may be an extra stroke before tathā (likewise), the natural opener of a further class. Conjectural, flagged as possible and hedged in both translations. 'saṃkīrṇā' for saṃkīrṇāḥ before g-: regular sandhi. 'grathita' is a recognised variant of granthita; no flag. 'kṛtya' = to be done; aśastrakṛtya = not to be done with the knife. Copula understood. The nouns are not stated (sirās understood). GROUPING: appears to continue line 38 (card 36).
lines_deva: नतथा क्षुद्रिकाः कुटिलाः संकीर्णा ग्रथिताः संधिषु चाशस्त्रकृत्याः
lines_iast: natathā kṣudrikāḥ kuṭilāḥ saṃkīrṇā grathitāḥ saṃdhiṣu cāśastrakṛtyāḥ

hindi: उनमें अपने-अपने अनुसार, चौथे अंश के विभाग से, पचहत्तर अधिक सौ का समूह वात और रक्त का वहन करता है।
english: Of them, each according to its own, by a division into fourth parts, a set of a hundred with seventy-five in addition carries Vāta and blood (anila-rakta).
notes: 175 is a quarter of the 700 of line 4 (card 4). 'anilaraktam' is read as a dvandva, Vāta and blood; a reading as one compound (blood with Vāta) is possible and is not decided. anila = wind, here Vāta. The sentence is not extended beyond what is printed.
lines_deva: तासां यथास्वं तुर्यांशविभागेन पंचसप्तत्यधिकं शतकमनिलरक्तं वहति
lines_iast: tāsāṃ yathāsvaṃ turyāṃśavibhāgena paṃcasaptatyadhikaṃ śatakamanilaraktaṃ vahati

hindi: यह विभाग पित्त, श्लेष्मा यानी कफ और शुद्ध रक्त में भी है। इस प्रकार स्थित रहते हुए दोष शरीर पर अनुग्रह करते हैं यानी उसे सहारा देते हैं।
english: This division is also in Pitta, śleṣman (Kapha) and pure blood. The doṣas, remaining thus, favour (support) the body.
notes: [02.06.41] Copula understood. 'eṣa' for eṣaḥ before v-: regular. śleṣman = Kapha (standard). What exactly the division of 175 is here (one quarter each for Vāta with blood, Pitta, śleṣman and pure blood) is suggested by the arithmetic with line 40 (card 38) but is not stated, so nothing is added. GROUPING: appears to complete line 40 (card 38). [02.06.42] 'evam' (thus) points back to a statement outside this unit; the state of the doṣas is not described here. 'sthitāḥ hi' is written sthitā hi by regular sandhi. anugṛhṇanti = favour, help, sustain; 'support' is the plain sense.

hindi: किन्तु व्यत्यय यानी उलट से पीड़ा देते हैं।
english: But by reversal (vyatyaya) they afflict.
notes: Elliptical: the subject (the doṣas of 42) is carried over and not supplied; no object is stated. vyatyaya = reversal, inversion, the contrary (of the state in 42).

hindi: वहाँ श्याव यानी साँवली-भूरी और अरुण यानी लाल, फड़कने वाली, सूक्ष्म, क्षण में भरी और क्षण में खाली, वात-रक्त को वहन करती हैं।
english: There, the dusky-brown and reddish, throbbing, fine (ones), momentarily full and momentarily empty, carry Vāta-blood (vāta-rakta).
notes: The adjectives are feminine plural and stand for an unstated feminine noun (dhamanī or sirā are both feminine); the noun is not given here, so none is supplied. 'riktā vāta-' is regular sandhi (riktāḥ + vāta-). vāta-rakta is read here as 'blood of the Vāta type' (the series 44-48 classifies blood by doṣa, ending with 'pure blood'); it is probably not the disease vātarakta (probable, not certain). śyāva = dusky/dark brown, aruṇa = reddish.
lines_deva: तत्र श्यावारुणाः प्रस्पंदिन्यः सूक्ष्माः क्षणपूर्णरिक्ता वातरक्तं वहंति
lines_iast: tatra śyāvāruṇāḥ praspaṃdinyaḥ sūkṣmāḥ kṣaṇapūrṇariktā vātaraktaṃ vahaṃti

hindi: नीली, पीली और काली, स्पर्श में उष्ण, शीघ्र स्रवित होने वाली: पित्त-रक्त। गोरी, स्निग्ध यानी चिकनी, स्थिर, ठण्डी, खुजली वाली: कफ-रक्त।
english: Blue, yellow and dark (ones), warm to the touch, quickly discharging: Pitta-blood (pitta-rakta). Fair, unctuous, steady, cold, itching (ones): Kapha-blood (kapha-rakta).
notes: [02.06.45] Elliptical: the verb vahanti (carry) is carried from 44 and is not supplied; the unstated noun is shown as '(ones)'. The three colours are read as a dvandva (blue, yellow and dark); asita = dark/black. srāvin = discharging, oozing (what is discharged is not stated). [02.06.46] Elliptical: the verb vahanti (carry) is carried from 44 and is not supplied; the unstated noun is shown as '(ones)'. gaurī = fair, whitish-yellow (the plain sense 'fair' is kept). kaṇḍūmatī = having itching (kaṇḍū); whose itching is not stated.
lines_deva: गौर्यः स्निग्धाः स्थिराः शीताः कंडूमत्यः कफरक्तं
lines_iast: gauryaḥ snigdhāḥ sthirāḥ śītāḥ kaṃḍūmatyaḥ kapharaktaṃ

hindi: लक्षणों के मिश्रण में: संसर्ग यानी मेल और सन्निपात यानी संयोग का रक्त। समान, गूढ़, स्निग्ध यानी चिकनी, रोहिणी यानी ऊपर चढ़ने वाली जिसका यहाँ अर्थ अनिश्चित है: शुद्ध रक्त।
english: In a mixture of the signs: blood of saṃsarga (combination) and sannipāta (union). Even, hidden, unctuous, rohiṇī (literally 'rising'; sense here uncertain) (ones): pure blood (śuddha-rakta).
notes: [02.06.47] Elliptical: the verb vahanti (carry) is carried from 44 and is not supplied. The compound saṃsarga-sannipāta-rakta is read as 'blood of saṃsarga and of sannipāta' (a dvandva joined to rakta); saṃsarga and sannipāta are the usual terms for combination of two doṣas and of all three, but the line itself does not count the doṣas, so the translation keeps the plain sense. [02.06.48] Elliptical: the verb vahanti (carry) is carried from 44 and is not supplied; the unstated noun is shown as '(ones)'. The print joins two words (samāgūḍhāḥ = samāḥ gūḍhāḥ by regular sandhi, a spacing slip; no flag); 'snigdhā rohiṇyaḥ' is likewise snigdhāḥ rohiṇyaḥ. rohiṇī is not enriched: it can mean rising/growing (or red); the sense in this list is uncertain. The closing 'iti' ends the five-fold list of 44-48 and is not translated.

words.gloss: dhamanīs (vessels, channels; probably blood vessels, probable)

hindi: धमनियाँ यानी सम्भवतः रक्तवाहिकाएँ तो चौबीस हैं।
english: The dhamanīs (vessels, probably blood vessels), however, are twenty-four.
notes: Copula understood. dhamanī = vessel or channel; the reading 'blood vessel' is probable, and whether artery is meant specifically is disputed. The count twenty-four is translated as printed (it agrees with the 10 + 10 + 4 of line 53 (card 47)).

hindi: इनसे यह शरीर, जल ले जाने वालियों से उद्यान की तरह और कुल्याओं यानी नहरों से खेत की तरह, आर्द्र होता है।
english: By these, this body is moistened, like a garden by water-carrying (ones) and like a field by canals (kulyā).
notes: 'tābhiḥ' (by them) refers back to the dhamanīs of 49. 'jalahāriṇībhiḥ' is feminine and qualifies an unstated noun, shown as '(ones)'. 'ārāmaḥ iva' is written ārāma iva by regular sandhi; the avagraha in kāyo'yam is the usual ayam after -o. upasnihyati is an active form, 'becomes moist'; 'is moistened' is the natural English with an agent.
lines_deva: ताभिःकायोऽयमाराम इव जलहारिणीभिः केदार इव कुल्याभिरुपस्निह्यति
lines_iast: tābhiḥkāyo'yamārāma iva jalahāriṇībhiḥ kedāra iva kulyābhirupasnihyati

hindi: और इनसे नाभि घिरी हुई है, अनुमानित पाठ पर चक्र की नाभि के अरों से घिरे होने के समान।
english: And by these the navel is surrounded, on a conjectural reading like the hub of a wheel by its spokes.

text_flags.why: possible: 'āraikariva' is not a word; 'arair iva' (like by spokes) fits the wheel-hub simile and the sense of 'āvṛtā'; the extra 'ka' and the long ā look like print slips

notes: The printed string 'āraikariva' cannot be parsed as it stands; 'arair iva' (like by spokes) is a conjectural restoration that suits the wheel-hub simile and the following 'āvṛtā' (the extra 'ka' looks like a print slip). Marked conjectural in both translations. 'cakranābhi' is taken as the hub of a wheel; 'āvṛtā' agrees with nābhiḥ (feminine). Copula understood.

hindi: इस कारण नाभि में विशेष रूप से प्राण स्थित हैं; और क्योंकि वह, अनुमानित पाठ पर, भीतर भी अधिष्ठान यानी आधार है। उन धमनियों में निश्चय ही, अनुमानित पाठ पर, दस ऊपर की ओर फैली हैं, दस नीचे की ओर और चार तिरछी।
english: Therefore the prāṇas (vital breaths) are established especially in the navel; and since it, on a conjectural reading, is also within a seat (adhiṣṭhāna) Of those dhamanīs indeed, on a conjectural reading, ten have spread upward, ten downward, four crosswise.

text_flags.why: possible: 'sāṃ' with ṃ is unexplained; sā antar api adhiṣṭhānam ('it also within is a seat') gives a construable reading; the anusvara looks like a print slip
possible: 'ddha' for 'da' and 'au' for 'o' are typical print errors; daśa ūrdhvam ('ten upward') parallels 'daśādhaḥ' (ten downward) and 'catasras tiryak' and gives the total of 24
possible: pra-mṛta means 'dead' and does not fit; pra-sṛta 'spread out' fits vessels, and sa/ma are confusable in this print

notes: [02.06.52] GROUPING: appears to continue in 53; the 'yataḥ' clause has no main clause in this unit, so the English is left open. The last token 'sāṃ'tarapyadhiṣṭhānaṃ' is read as sā antar api adhiṣṭhānam (the printed ṃ before the avagraha looks like a slip); 'sā' is taken to be the navel (feminine), which is a conjecture, hence conjectural marks and low confidence. 'viśeṣeṇaprāṇā' = viśeṣeṇa prāṇāḥ (spacing slip). prāṇa: kept as 'prāṇa (vital breath)'; no modern equivalent forced. [02.06.53] GROUPING: appears to continue 52. Two print damages, both conjectural: 'ddhaśaurdhvaṃ' read as daśa ūrdhvam (dd/d and au/o confusions) and 'pramṛtā' read as prasṛtāḥ (pra-mṛta would mean 'dead'; sa/ma confusion). The reading is supported by the total: ten + ten + four = twenty-four, the number given in 49. The nouns for 'ten', 'four' are the dhamanīs; the numerals are translated as printed.
lines_deva: तासां खलु धमनीनां द्धशौर्ध्वं प्रमृता दशाधश्चतस्रस्तिर्यक्
lines_iast: tāsāṃ khalu dhamanīnāṃ ddhaśaurdhvaṃ pramṛtā daśādhaścatasrastiryak

hindi: तब उनसे अपने-अपने अनुसार अंग और अवयव धारण किए जाते हैं और पुष्ट किए जाते हैं। इनमें से ऊपर जाने वाली हृदय तक पहुँचकर प्रत्येक तीन प्रकार की हो जाती हैं।
english: Then, by them, the limbs and parts, each according to its own, are held and nourished. Of these, the upward-going (ones), having reached the heart (hṛdaya), each come to be threefold.

text_flags.why: possible: aṅga + avayava should contract to aṅgāvayava; the long ā-mātra is missing in the print (words keep the two members aṅga-avayavāḥ)

notes: [02.06.54] 'tataḥ' (then, thence) is kept in its plain sense; it may also be read as 'therefore'. 'avayavāḥ dhāryante' is written avayavā dhāryante by regular sandhi. 'aṅgāvayavāḥ' is read as 'limbs and parts', each limb with its parts. [02.06.55] The three kinds are not named in this unit (the next unit counts thirty). 'ūrdhvagāḥ hṛdayam' is written ūrdhvagā hṛdayam by regular sandhi.

words.gloss: Vāta; Pitta; Kapha; blood (rakta); rasa (the nutrient fluid, first dhātu; standard)
carrying (on a possible correction; printed vahantaḥ)

hindi: फिर तीस के बीच दो-दो वात, पित्त, कफ, रक्त और रस यानी पोषक द्रव को वहन करने वाली।
english: Then, among the thirty, two and two, carrying Vāta, Pitta, Kapha, blood (rakta) and rasa (the nutrient fluid).

text_flags.why: possible: 'dve dve' is feminine, so the participle should be feminine (vahantyaḥ); printed masculine vahantaḥ looks like a slip

notes: GROUPING: appears to begin a list that continues through 57-59 (the thirty are 10 + 8 + 8 + 4). There is no finite verb, only the participle; 'dve dve' is read as 'two each' over the five items. The printed 'vahantaḥ' is masculine plural and does not agree with the feminine 'dve dve' (expected vahantyaḥ); flagged as possible. 'vāta, pitta, kapha' are the doṣas; 'rasa' here is the nutrient fluid (dhātu), not taste. Alternative conjecture: vahataḥ (3 du., 'two and two carry'), one anusvāra off the print and parallel to the finite verbs of 59 and 62; vahantyaḥ remains possible.

hindi: आठ से शब्द, रूप, रस यानी स्वाद और गन्ध ग्रहण किए जाते हैं।
english: By eight, sound, form, taste and smell are grasped (perceived).
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 56. Only four of the sense-objects are listed (touch is not named in this line). 'rūpa' = form (visible appearance); 'rasa' here is taste. 'gandhāḥ gṛhyante' is written gandhā gṛhyante by regular sandhi.

hindi: दो-दो से बोलता है, घोष यानी ध्वनि करता है, सोता है और जागता है। दो आँसू वहन करती हैं; और स्तनों पर आश्रित दो: नारी का स्तन्य यानी दूध, नर का शुक्र यानी वीर्य नामक प्रजनन-द्रव।
english: By two and two, one speaks, makes a sound (ghoṣa), sleeps and wakes. Two carry tears; and two, resting on the breasts: a woman's milk (stanya), a man's semen (śukra).
notes: [02.06.58] GROUPING: appears to continue 56-57. The repeated 'dvābhyām' is read as distributive (two for each of the four acts, which gives eight). The text does not say which pair serves which act; the subject of the verbs is unstated. ghoṣa = sound, cry; its exact sense beside 'speaks' is not fixed. [02.06.59] GROUPING: appears to complete the list of 56-58 (two for tears and two on the breasts make the last four of the thirty). Elliptical: for the second pair the verb vahataḥ (carry) is carried over and not supplied. 'nāryāḥ stanyam' is the printed joined form (nāryāḥstanyaṃ), a spacing slip.
lines_deva: द्वाभ्यां द्वाभ्यां भाषते घोषं करोति स्वपिति प्रतिबुध्यते च
द्वे चाश्रु वहतः द्वे च स्तनाश्रिते नार्याःस्तन्यं नरस्य शुक्रं
lines_iast: dvābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ bhāṣate ghoṣaṃ karoti svapiti pratibudhyate ca
dve cāśru vahataḥ dve ca stanāśrite nāryāḥstanyaṃ narasya śukraṃ

hindi: नीचे जाने वाली, पक्वाशय यानी सम्भवतः बड़ी आँत के क्षेत्र में स्थित, इसी प्रकार तीन प्रकार की हो जाती हैं।
english: The downward-going (ones), situated in the pakvāśaya (the seat of digested matter, probably the large intestine region), likewise come to be threefold.
notes: The 'ones' are presumably the ten downward dhamanīs of 53, but the line itself does not name them. pakvāśaya = seat of the digested/ripened (food, stool): probably the colon/large-intestine region (probable). 'pakvāśayasthāḥ evam' is written pakvāśayasthā evam by regular sandhi.

hindi: वहाँ पहली दस: पहले के समान।
english: There, the first ten: as before.
notes: Elliptical and unclear: 'daśādyāḥ' is read as daśa ādyāḥ, 'the first ten', presumably of the thirty that arise from the downward group (60), and 'pūrvavat' as 'as before' (as in the upward group); neither referent is stated, so no verb or noun is supplied. 'daśādyāḥ' could also mean 'ten and so on'.

hindi: दो अन्न वहन करती हैं, आँतों के आश्रय से; दो जल, दो मूत्र; दो शुक्र यानी वीर्य नामक प्रजनन-द्रव वहन करती हैं; और दो छोड़ती हैं।
english: Two carry food, with the intestines (antra) as their resting-place; two, water; two, urine; two carry semen (śukra); and two release.
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 60-61. For the 2nd, 3rd pairs the verb vahataḥ is carried over and not supplied. 'vahataḥ annam' is written vahato 'nnam by regular sandhi. The object of 'muñcataḥ' is not stated and is not supplied. 'antrāśrayeṇa' (instrumental) is read as 'having the intestines as resting-place'; it may qualify the food-carrying pair only.
lines_deva: द्वे वहतोऽन्नमंत्राश्रयेण द्वे तोयं द्वे मूत्रं द्वे शुक्रंवहतो द्वे च मुंचतः
lines_iast: dve vahato'nnamaṃtrāśrayeṇa dve toyaṃ dve mūtraṃ dve śukraṃvahato dve ca muṃcataḥ

hindi: वे ही दोनों: नारियों का आर्तव यानी रजोरक्त।
english: Those very two: of women, ārtava (menstrual blood).
notes: Elliptical: the verb (carry) is carried from 62 and is not supplied. 'te' probably refers to the pair that carries śukra in 62 (the parallel with 59), but the line does not say so.

words.gloss: thick, large; intestine; bound to, connected with

hindi: दो मल को बाहर निकालने वाली, अनुमानित पाठ पर, स्थूल आँत से बँधी; शेष आठ तिरछी जाने वाली स्वेद को तृप्त करती हैं।
english: Two that expel stool (varcas, on a conjectural reading), bound to the large intestine (sthūlāntra); but the remaining eight, running crosswise, satiate the sweat (sveda).

text_flags.why: possible: vajra ('thunderbolt') gives no sense here; varcas (stool) + nirasanī (expelling) with 'sthūlāntrapratibaddhe' fits the group of passages in 62; jr/rc is a plausible misreading

notes: The printed 'vajrronirasanyau' is read as varcas-nirasanyau ('expelling stool'): vajra (thunderbolt) gives no sense, and a stool-expelling pair bound to the large intestine fits the list of 62; conjectural, flagged. Hindi 'तृप्त करती हैं' keeps the literal 'satiate'; 'nourish' is the English sense (abhitarpayanti). The 'remaining eight' presumably complete a count not given in this line.
lines_deva: द्वे वज्र्रोनिरसन्यौ स्थूलांत्रप्रतिबद्धे शेषास्त्वष्टौ तिरश्चीनाः स्वेदमभितर्पयंति
lines_iast: dve vajrronirasanyau sthūlāṃtrapratibaddhe śeṣāstvaṣṭau tiraścīnāḥ svedamabhitarpayaṃti

words.gram: pres. pass. part. √bhid, f. nom. pl.

words.gloss: become (on a possible correction; printed bhavati)

hindi: तिरछी जाने वाली चार विभक्त होती हुई बहुत प्रकार की हो जाती हैं, यह पहले कहा जा चुका है।
english: The four that go crosswise, being divided, become very manifold (in very many ways); this was stated before.

text_flags.why: possible: the subject 'catasraḥ ... bhidyamānāḥ' is plural, so the verb should be bhavanti; the singular looks like a print slip

notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 64. The back-reference is probably to the 'four crosswise' of 53, though 'prāk' could point to an earlier chapter. The printed 'bhavati' is singular beside a plural subject; read as bhavanti, flagged as possible. 'iti uktam' is taken as 'this has been said'.

words.gloss: blood; path, passage (probably the passage of the menstrual blood)

hindi: पुरुषों के स्रोतस यानी शरीर के मार्ग नौ हैं: दो कान, दो नेत्र, दो नासापुट, मुख, पायु यानी गुदा और मूत्रमार्ग; और तीन अन्य स्त्रियों के: दोनों स्तन और रक्तपथ यानी सम्भवतः रजोरक्त का मार्ग।
english: The srotas (bodily channels, openings) of men are nine: the two ears, two eyes, two nostrils, mouth, anus (pāyu) and urinary passage; and three other (ones) of women: the two breasts and the blood-passage (rakta-patha, probably the passage of the menstrual blood).
notes: Copula understood. The nine are counted as listed: 2 + 2 + 2 + 1 + 1 + 1. 'anyāni trīṇi' (three others) are then the women's: two breasts and the blood-passage. rakta-patha is not explained in the line; 'passage of the menstrual blood' is probable, not certain. pāyu = anus (standard). srotas is kept as a doctrinal term (channel).
lines_deva: स्रोतांसि पुंसांनव कर्णौ नेत्रे नासापुटौ मुखं पायुर्मूत्रपथो ऽन्यानि च त्रीणि स्त्रीणांस्तनौ रक्तपथश्च
lines_iast: srotāṃsi puṃsāṃnava karṇau netre nāsāpuṭau mukhaṃ pāyurmūtrapatho 'nyāni ca trīṇi strīṇāṃstanau raktapathaśca

words.gloss: prāṇa (vital breath); water; food; dhātu; mala

hindi: तथा अन्य भीतरी स्रोतस: जीवन के आयतन यानी आश्रय, तेरह; प्राण, जल, अन्न, धातु और मल के आयतन।
english: And the other inner srotas (channels): seats (āyatana) of life, thirteen; seats of prāṇa (vital breath), water, food, the dhātus and the malas.
notes: The avagraha in tathā'parāṇi is the print habit (ā + a gives ā). Copula understood. 'trayodaśa' (thirteen) is translated as printed; the line does not list the thirteen (the lines 68-82 (card 60/73) name some). The two predicates ('seats of life' and 'seats of prāṇa, water, food, dhātus and malas') are read as describing the same srotas. dhātu and mala are doctrinal terms and are kept without a modern equivalent.

hindi: वहाँ प्राण को वहन करने वालों का मूल हृदय और महास्रोतस है।
english: There, of the prāṇa-carrying (ones), the root (mūla) is the heart (hṛdaya) and the great channel (mahāsrotas).
notes: The 'prāṇa-carrying (ones)' are the prāṇavaha srotas of 67, left as an unstated noun. mahāsrotas is kept literally ('great channel'); its identification is disputed and is not given in the line. mahāsrotas (disputed): in Caraka-type usage the great channel is the alimentary tract (koṣṭha); some commentators take the large vessels at the heart; unresolved here, so the term is kept untranslated beyond 'great channel'.

words.gloss: exertion (the word continues in the next token)
urge; holding back; and the rest

hindi: वे क्षय, रूक्षता, प्यास, भूख, व्यायाम, वेगों को रोकने आदि से दूषित होते हैं।
english: They become vitiated by wasting (kṣaya), dryness (raukṣya), thirst, hunger, exertion (vyāyāma), holding back of urges (vega-dhāraṇa) and the like.
notes: The print breaks the word vyāyāma across two tokens (vyāyā | mavega-): a spacing slip, no flag; the 'ma' is read with the first word. 'tāni' refers to the prāṇa-carrying srotas of 68. kṣaya = wasting, loss (not the disease name, in this list of causes). vega-dhāraṇa = holding back natural urges.

hindi: तब उच्छ्वसन यानी साँस: अतिसृष्ट यानी अधिक छूटती हुई, रुकी हुई, कुपित, थोड़ी-थोड़ी या बार-बार, शब्द और पीड़ा सहित।
english: Then breathing (ucchvasana): excessively released, obstructed, agitated, scanty or frequent, with sound and pain.
notes: No finite verb; the adjectives are neuter and agree with ucchvasanam. The single 'vā' follows the last pair, so 'scanty or frequent' is the natural grouping; whether 'or' also runs through the earlier terms is not settled by the wording. 'saśabdaśūla' is read as 'with sound and pain'; it could also be 'with noisy pain'. 'alpālpam' = alpa-alpam, 'little by little, scanty'.

words.gloss: like śvāsa (breathlessness; dyspnoea or asthma-type, probable)

hindi: वहाँ साधन यानी चिकित्सा श्वास यानी साँस फूलने की बीमारी के समान, सम्भवतः दमा।
english: There, the treatment (sādhana) is as in śvāsa (breathlessness; probably dyspnoea of the asthma type).
notes: Copula understood. śvāsa = laboured breathing; reading it as the breathlessness disorder (asthma/dyspnoea type) is probable. The text refers to the treatment given elsewhere for śvāsa; it is not repeated here. 'sādhana' = means of accomplishing, treatment.

hindi: जल को वहन करने वालों का मूल तालु और क्लोम है, जिसकी पहचान विवादित है।
english: Of the water-carrying (ones), the root is the palate (tālu) and the kloma (identity disputed).
notes: kloma (kloman) is not identified in the line; the pancreas, the right lung and the trachea/throat have each been proposed (disputed), so it is kept as 'kloma'. 'kloma ca' is printed run together (klomaca). The unstated noun is shown as '(ones)'.

words.gloss: āma (undigested; sense uncertain here); fear; excessive drinking; heat; dry; food; holding back of thirst (on a conjectural reading); and the rest

hindi: वे आम यानी अपक्व या कच्चा जिसका यहाँ अर्थ अनिश्चित है, भय, अतिपान, उष्ण, सूखा अन्न, अनुमानित पाठ पर तृष्णा के निग्रह यानी रोकने आदि से दूषित होते हैं। तब अत्यधिक प्यास, मुख का सूखना, कानों में भनभनाहट और अँधेरा दिखना।
english: They become vitiated by āma (sense uncertain here), fear, excessive drinking, heat, dry food, holding back of thirst (on a conjectural reading) and the like. Then excessive thirst, dryness of the mouth, ringing (kṣveḍana, probably tinnitus-type) in the ears and seeing of darkness.

text_flags.why: possible: 'tṛṣṇi-' is not a stem; tṛṣṇā-nigraha ('holding back of thirst') is a natural cause for the water channels, and the dropped 'ān' is a plausible print slip

notes: 'tāni' refers to the water-carrying srotas of 72. 'āma' is kept unexplained (undigested matter or 'raw' are possible; the sense here is uncertain). The printed 'tṛṣṇigraha' is not a regular compound; read as tṛṣṇā-nigraha (holding back of thirst), a conjecture (flagged). 'atipāna' = excessive drinking (of what is not stated). kṣveḍana = humming/ringing sound; the tinnitus-type sense is probable. The list of signs has no verb.

hindi: वहाँ तृष्णा में कही गई औषध।
english: There, the medicine (auṣadha) stated for thirst (tṛṣṇā).
notes: Elliptical: no verb; 'the medicine said for thirst' refers to the treatment given elsewhere, which is not repeated here. tṛṣṇā = thirst.

words.gloss: āmāśaya (seat of undigested food; probably the stomach)
Mātrāśitīya (name of a chapter, literally on the measure of what is eaten); said, stated

hindi: अन्न को वहन करने वालों का मूल आमाशय यानी सम्भवतः जठर है, और बायाँ पार्श्व। उनके दूषित होने पर सब कुछ मात्राशितीय में कहा हुआ जानना चाहिए।
english: Of the food-carrying (ones), the root is the āmāśaya (seat of undigested food, probably the stomach) and the left side (vāma-pārśva). In their vitiation, one should understand all as stated in the Mātrāśitīya.
notes: [02.06.75] The unstated noun is shown as '(ones)'. āmāśaya = seat of āma (the unprocessed food): probably the stomach (probable). 'vāma-pārśva' = the left side (flank); not further specified. [02.06.76] 'Mātrāśitīya' is taken as the name of a chapter (probably an earlier chapter of this work); the line does not say which, and it is not checked here. 'duṣṭau' = in vitiation (locative of duṣṭi).

hindi: रस को वहन करने वालों का मूल हृदय और दस धमनियाँ हैं।
english: Of the rasa-carrying (ones), the root is the heart (hṛdaya) and the ten dhamanīs (vessels).
notes: The unstated noun is shown as '(ones)'. The ten dhamanīs are probably those of 53 and 55 (the upward ten that reach the heart), but the line does not say so. 'rasa' is the nutrient fluid (dhātu).

hindi: रक्त को वहन करने वालों के यकृत और प्लीहा।
english: Of the blood-carrying (ones): the liver (yakṛt) and the spleen (plīhan).
notes: Elliptical: 'mūlam' (root) is carried over from 77 and is not supplied; the unstated noun is shown as '(ones)'. 'yakṛt plīhā' are two words (yakṛt, plīhan nominative).

hindi: मांस को वहन करने वालों के स्नाव यानी सम्भवतः स्नायु या कण्डरा और त्वचा।
english: Of the flesh-carrying (ones): the sinews (snāva, probably tendons or ligaments) and the skin (tvac).
notes: Elliptical: 'mūlam' is carried over from 77 and is not supplied; the unstated noun is shown as '(ones)'. snāva (n.) is the print's form for sinew; probably the same as snāyu (probable).

hindi: मेद यानी वसा को वहन करने वालों के दोनों वृक्क यानी गुर्दे और मांस।
english: Of the fat-carrying (ones) (medas): the two kidneys (vṛkka) and the flesh (māṃsa).
notes: Elliptical: 'mūlam' is carried over from 77 and is not supplied; the unstated noun is shown as '(ones)'. 'medovāhinām vṛkkau' is printed run together (medovāhināṃvṛkkau), a spacing slip. medas = fat (standard).

hindi: अस्थि को वहन करने वालों के जघन यानी सम्भवतः कूल्हा या कमर का क्षेत्र और मेद।
english: Of the bone-carrying (ones): the jaghana (hips or loins region, probable) and fat (medas).
notes: Elliptical: 'mūlam' is carried over from 77 and is not supplied; the unstated noun is shown as '(ones)'. jaghana is the hip or loin region, which part exactly is not stated (probable).

hindi: मज्जा को वहन करने वालों के पर्व यानी जोड़ और अस्थियाँ।
english: Of the marrow-carrying (ones): the joints (parvan) and the bones (asthi).
notes: Elliptical: 'mūlam' is carried over from 77 and is not supplied; the unstated noun is shown as '(ones)'. The unit ends the list printed here; the later dhātu (śukra) and mala carriers are not in this chunk.

hindi: शुक्र यानी वीर्य को वहन करने वालों के दोनों स्तन, दोनों मुष्क यानी अण्डकोश और मज्जा।
english: Of those that carry śukra (semen): the two breasts, the two testicles (muṣka) and the marrow (majjā).

text_flags.why: possible: the compound is śukra-vāhin (carrier of semen); the r is missing in print

notes: Printed 'śukavāhināṃ' for śukravāhinām (r dropped), possible print slip. Elliptical: 'of the srotas' / 'the root is' is carried from lines 77-82 (card 68/73) and not supplied; the genitive is read as 'of the carriers of semen'. Whether 'carriers' are the channels (srotas) is understood from the context. The breasts are listed among semen carriers as printed; not corrected.

hindi: मूत्र को वहन करने वालों की बस्ति यानी मूत्राशय और दोनों वंक्षण यानी जाँघ के जोड़।
english: Of those that carry urine: the bladder (basti) and the two groins (vaṅkṣaṇa).
notes: Printed 'mūtravāhināṃbastir' joins two words; split without a flag as a spacing slip. basti = bladder here (the urinary bag), not the enema device. Elliptical: the 'root' is carried from lines 77-82 (card 68/73) and not supplied.

words.gloss: digested (pakva); seat (āśaya); pakvāśaya = the lower seat of digested food, large-bowel region (probable)

hindi: मल को वहन करने वालों का पक्वाशय यानी पचे हुए का स्थान, सम्भवतः बड़ी आँत का क्षेत्र और स्थूलान्त्र यानी सम्भवतः बड़ी आँत।
english: Of those that carry dung (śakṛt): the pakvāśaya (seat of the digested, probably the large-bowel region) and the thick intestine (sthūlāntra, probably the large intestine).
notes: pakvāśaya and sthūlāntra identified with the large-bowel region and large intestine: probable. Elliptical: the 'root' is carried from lines 77-82 (card 68/73) and not supplied.

hindi: स्वेद यानी पसीने को वहन करने वालों का मेद यानी चर्बी और रोमकूप यानी रोम के छिद्र।
english: Of those that carry sweat (sveda): the fat (medas) and the hair-pores (romakūpa).
notes: Printed 'svedavāhināṃmedo' joins two words (sandhi -ṃ + m); split without a flag. Elliptical: the 'root' is carried from lines 77-82 (card 68/73) and not supplied.

words.gram: tat-puruṣa (with dvandva vṛddhi-kṣaya), n. inst. sg.

hindi: इनके अनेक तरह के दूषण, अहितकर आहार और विहार यानी आचरण, उपद्रव और साधन को दोष आदि से जानना चाहिए; अपने-अपने अनुसार वृद्धि और क्षय के लक्षण से पहचानना चाहिए।
english: Of these, the various vitiation, the unwholesome food and conduct (vihāra), the complications (upadrava) and the treatment one should know through the doṣa and the rest; one should discern each by the sign of increase and decrease.
notes: The syntax is loose: 'doṣādivijñānīyāt' is read as doṣa-ādi + vijñānīyāt ('one should know ... by/as doṣa and the rest'); the instrument of knowing is not stated, so the translation keeps 'through' only as the plainest reading. Alternative: 'one should know the doṣa and the rest' as objects. 'yathāsvam' is placed with the final verb. Printed 'vijñānīyādyathāsvaṃ' joins the verb and the adverb (sandhi t + y -> d y). Alternative: 'vividham' (n. acc. sg.) may agree with 'ahitāhāravihāram' ('various unwholesome food and conduct') instead of qualifying 'dūṣaṇam'.
lines_deva: तेषां दूषणं विविधमहिताहारविहारमुपद्रवान् साधनं च दोषादिविज्ञानीयाद्यथास्वं वृद्धिक्षयलक्षणेन लक्षयेत्
lines_iast: teṣāṃ dūṣaṇaṃ vividhamahitāhāravihāramupadravān sādhanaṃ ca doṣādivijñānīyādyathāsvaṃ vṛddhikṣayalakṣaṇena lakṣayet

words.gloss: unclear (probably rudhira-śruti, flow of blood, with a stray 'ani')

hindi: स्रोतस् के वेध पर तो भ्रम, मोह, कम्प, प्रलाप, आध्मान, शूल, अरुचि, प्यास, वमन, ज्वर, अनुमानित पाठ पर रक्त का बहना, मूत्र और मल का रुकना, और मृत्यु।
english: But on the piercing of the srotas (channels): giddiness, fainting or confusion, tremor, raving, distension of the belly (ādhmāna), pain, distaste for food, thirst, vomiting, fever, on a conjectural reading flow of blood, retention of urine and stool, and death.

text_flags.why: possible: 'ani' after jvara has no clear sense; rudhira-śruti (blood flow) fits the list

notes: Damaged print: 'jvarānirudhiraśruti' is read on a conjecture as jvara + (a stray 'ani') + rudhira-śruti (flow of blood); the stray syllables are left unexplained and the 'ani' is kept unsplit as unclear. The list is read as nominatives plural/singular without a verb ('result' is understood). 'moha' = fainting or confusion. 'srotas' is a doctrinal term (body channel), kept.

hindi: इसलिए स्रोतस् में विद्ध को अस्वीकार करके उपचार करना चाहिए। और जिसका शल्य निकाला जा चुका हो उसका सद्योव्रण की विधि से।
english: Therefore, having refused one pierced in a srotas, one should treat (him). And (one) whose dart has been extracted, by the procedure for a fresh wound.

text_flags.why: possible: srotas + viddha gives srotoviddha; 'au' is a print slip

notes: [02.06.89] Printed 'srotauviddhaṃ' is read as srotoviddham (srotas-viddha); the 'au' looks like a print slip. 'pratyākhyāya' = having declined (the case as hopeless); that one then treats is as stated. The object 'him' is understood. Alternative emendation: 'srotasi viddham' (pierced in the srotas); sense the same. [02.06.90] Elliptical: the verb 'one should treat' is carried from line 89 (card 80) and is not supplied; the unstated noun is shown as '(one)'. GROUPING: appears to continue 89.

hindi: उनमें सिराएँ यानी सम्भवतः शिराएँ यानी नसें और धमनियाँ यानी स्पन्दन करने वाली वाहिकाएँ, सम्भवतः आधुनिक अर्थ की धमनियाँ, स्रोतसों के ही विशेष रूप हैं।
english: Among these, the sirā (vessels, probably veins) and the dhamanī (pulsating vessels, probably arteries) are particular forms of the srotas only.
notes: sirā and dhamanī: modern equivalents (vein, artery) are probable, not exact. The copula is understood. Printed 'sirā' is sirāḥ (visarga lost before dh, regular sandhi), plural like dhamanyaḥ.

hindi: परन्तु दूसरे अन्यता यानी भिन्नता मानते हैं।
english: But others maintain a difference (anyatva).
notes: 'anyatvam' = otherness; 'icchanti' = they wish/maintain. The 'they' (sirā, dhamanī, srotas) is understood. The printed 'anyetvanyatvam' = anye tu anyatvam.

hindi: सिरा, धमनी और स्रोतसों में केवल परस्पर निकटता, समान कर्म और सूक्ष्मता के कारण, भिन्न कर्म वाले होते हुए भी, मानो भेद का अभाव दिखाई देता है।
english: Merely through mutual proximity, similarity of function and fineness, a non-distinction, as it were, is perceived among the sirā, dhamanī and srotas, even though their functions are distinct.
notes: Printed 'avibhāgaiva' is read as avibhāga + iva (spacing slip; the Devanagari prints अविभाग इव with the vowels unjoined, the IAST 'ai' is a transliteration artefact). 'kevalam' taken with the reasons. Only a view being reported (see 92, 94).

hindi: दूसरे फिर कहते हैं।
english: Others, again, say:
notes: Opens the next view; the quotation follows in line 95 (card 85). GROUPING: appears to introduce 95.

words.gloss: rasa (the first dhātu; plasma-like fluid); carrying

hindi: स्रोतस्, सिराएँ, धमनियाँ, रसवाहिनियाँ, नाड़ियाँ, पन्थ, अयन, मार्ग, शरीर के छिद्र, बन्द और खुले, स्थान, आशय यानी आधार, क्षय यानी निवास और निकेत यानी आवास: ये शरीर में धातुओं के दिखाई देने वाले और न दिखाई देने वाले अवकाशों के नाम हैं।
english: Srotas (channels), sirā, dhamanī, the carriers of rasa, nāḍī, paths, routes, ways, openings of the body, closed and open, places, seats (āśaya), abodes and dwellings: these are the names, in the body, of the spaces of the dhātus, perceptible and imperceptible.
notes: The words after 'rasavāhinyaḥ' are all nominative plural names in a list; 'saṃvṛtāsaṃvṛtāni' (closed and open) is read with 'śarīracchidrāṇi' (openings of the body); it could also be a separate name in the list. 'rasavāhinyaḥ' = the carriers of rasa (feminine plural: vessels). Printed 'kṣayā' = kṣayāḥ; 'paṃthāno'yanāni' = panthānaḥ ayanāni. The closing 'iti' is left to notes.
lines_deva: स्रोतांसि सिरा धमन्यो रसवाहिन्यो नाड्यः पंथानोऽयनानि मार्गाः शरीरच्छिद्राणि संवृतासंवृतानि स्थानान्याशयाः क्षया निकेताश्चेति शरीरे धात्ववकाशानां लक्ष्यालक्ष्याणां नामानीति
lines_iast: srotāṃsi sirā dhamanyo rasavāhinyo nāḍyaḥ paṃthāno'yanāni mārgāḥ śarīracchidrāṇi saṃvṛtāsaṃvṛtāni sthānānyāśayāḥ kṣayā niketāśceti śarīre dhātvavakāśānāṃ lakṣyālakṣyāṇāṃ nāmānīti

hindi: और वे अवकाश।
english: And these spaces.
notes: Subject of 97; the verb is in the next unit. GROUPING: appears to continue into 97.

hindi: प्रकुपित होकर वे अपने स्थान में स्थित और मार्ग में स्थित धातुओं को प्रकुपित करते हैं।
english: Agitated, they agitate the dhātus that stand in their seats and those that stand on their paths.

text_flags.why: possible: the repeated 'sthāna' may be a print slip

notes: Printed 'sthānasthānamārgasthāṃś' is read as sthāna-sthān + mārga-sthān ('sthāna' possibly repeated by a print slip). Alternative: sthāna-sthān + a-mārga-sthān ('in place and not on their path'), which also reproduces the print exactly; the first reading is kept as the plainer one.

hindi: वे भी उन्हें और स्रोतसों को।
english: They too (agitate) those and the srotas.
notes: Elliptical: the verb 'agitate' is carried from line 97 (card 87) and is not supplied. 'tān' = those dhātus (understood).

hindi: स्रोतस् और धातु धातुओं को।
english: The srotas and the dhātus (agitate) the dhātus.
notes: Elliptical: the verb 'agitate' is carried from line 97 (card 87) and is not supplied.

hindi: इन सबके ही दूषित करने वाले दूषित दोष हैं।
english: The vitiators of all these indeed are the vitiated doṣas.

text_flags.why: possible: -m + eva does not give 'aiva'; the 'ai' is a print slip

notes: Printed 'sarveṣāmaiva' is read as sarveṣām eva ('ai' for 'e' looks like a print slip). 'duṣṭā' = duṣṭāḥ (visarga dropped before d in print is regular). Alternative for the printed Devanagari 'सर्वेषामैव' (real ऐ): sarveṣāṃ caiva (ca lost); 'eva' kept as the simpler guess.

hindi: और वे अधिकतर अग्नि यानी पाचन की अग्नि के दोष से दूषित होते हैं।
english: And they mostly become vitiated through a fault of agni (the digestive fire).
notes: agni = digestive fire (doctrinal term, kept). The ablative 'agnidoṣāt' = from/through a fault of agni.

words.gloss: lifespan; health; strength; growth; complexion; ojas

hindi: इसलिए निमित्त: आयु, आरोग्य, बल, उपचय यानी वृद्धि, वर्ण यानी रंगत और ओजस् यानी जीवन-सार।
english: Therefore the causes (nimitta): lifespan, health, strength, growth, complexion and ojas (vital essence).
notes: The relation is not stated: nimittāni is neuter plural and the six items are also neuter plural; it is probably 'agni is the cause of lifespan ... and ojas', but no verb or genitive is given and none is supplied. ojas = vigour (doctrinal term, kept). Read as an incomplete statement.

words.gloss: bound to that; dependent on that
rañjaka (a kind of Pitta that colours); and the rest

hindi: और उसी पर आश्रित रञ्जक यानी पित्त का एक भेद आदि, भूताग्नियाँ यानी भूतों की अग्नियाँ और धात्वग्नियाँ यानी धातुओं की अग्नियाँ हैं। वैसे ही अन्न भी उसी से पचा हुआ अमृत भाव को प्राप्त होता है और बिना पचा विष भाव को।
english: And dependent on that alone are the rañjaka (a kind of Pitta) and the rest, the bhūtāgnis (fires of the elements) and the dhātvagnis (fires of the dhātus). Likewise food too, digested (pakva) by that very (agni), attains the state of nectar (amṛta), and undigested, the state of poison (viṣa).
notes: [02.06.103] 'tat' = that agni (understood). rañjaka is the colouring kind of Pitta (standard in later Āyurveda); 'and the rest' is not listed here. Neuter 'rañjakādīni' beside masculine agnis: the list is loose. Copula understood. [02.06.104] Printed 'pakka' = pakva (kk spelling; orthographic normalisation). 'tena' = by that agni (understood). The verb 'attains' serves both halves.

hindi: उनमें पित्त का विशेष रूप, जिसका नाम पाचक यानी पचाने वाला है, अग्नि है, ऐसा पहले कहा गया।
english: Among these, a special kind of Pitta, named pācaka (the digesting one), is agni: so it was stated earlier.
notes: 'iti' closes the quoted statement and is rendered 'so'. The earlier statement is in an earlier part of the work and is not checked here.

hindi: दूसरे फिर कहते हैं।
english: Others, again, say:
notes: Opens the next view; the statement follows in line 107 (card 96). GROUPING: appears to introduce 107.

words.gloss: doṣa; dhātu; mala (waste); coming together; produced by

hindi: दोष, धातु और मल यानी अपशिष्ट के संयोग से उत्पन्न भीतरी ऊष्मा, जिसका स्थान और कर्म पहले बताए अनुसार हैं, अग्नि है।
english: Agni is the inner heat produced by the coming together of doṣa, dhātu and mala, whose seat and function are as indicated.
notes: Closing 'iti' marks the end of the view reported. mala = waste product (doctrinal term). 'yathānirdiṣṭa' refers to earlier statements, not checked here.

words.gloss: āmāśaya (seat of the undigested; stomach, probable); staying in

hindi: वह अग्नि, यानी भीतरी अग्नि, विधि से खाए हुए अन्न को, जिसे प्राण वायु ने कोष्ठ यानी भण्डार या पेट में खींचा है, जिसका संघात द्रवों से टूट गया है, जिसे स्नेह यानी तेल या वसा से नरम किया गया है, समान वायु से प्रज्वलित होकर, आमाशय यानी कच्चे अन्न का स्थान, सम्भवतः जठर में स्थित को, हाँडी में स्थित पानी और चावल के समान, पकाता है।
english: That agni, the inner fire, kindled by samāna (wind), cooks the food eaten according to rule, drawn into the koṣṭha (storehouse, belly) by prāṇa wind, its mass broken apart by liquids, softened by sneha (oil or fat), lying in the āmāśaya (seat of the undigested, probably the stomach) like water and rice in a pot.
notes: The sentence is long; 'abhisandhukṣitaḥ' (kindled) qualifies agni. 'sthālīsthamivāṃbutaṇḍulam' = water and rice lying in a pot (dvandva). 'agniraṃtaragniḥ' read as agniḥ + antar-agniḥ (agni, the inner fire). The wind names prāṇa and samāna are doctrinal. āmāśaya = stomach: probable.
lines_deva: स खलु विधिवदभ्यवहृतमन्नजातंप्राणेन वायुना कोष्ठमाकृष्टं द्रवैर्विभिन्नसंघातं स्नेहेन मृदूकृतमभिसंधुक्षितः समानेनामाशयस्थं स्थालीस्थमिवांबुतंडुलमग्निरंतरग्निःपचति
lines_iast: sa khalu vidhivadabhyavahṛtamannajātaṃprāṇena vāyunā koṣṭhamākṛṣṭaṃ dravairvibhinnasaṃghātaṃ snehena mṛdūkṛtamabhisaṃdhukṣitaḥ samānenāmāśayasthaṃ sthālīsthamivāṃbutaṃḍulamagniraṃtaragniḥpacati

words.gram: pres. pass. part. √pac, n. nom. sg.
loc. sg. of ādi, as ind.

hindi: वह अन्न तो, सब रसों यानी स्वादों वाला होते हुए भी, पकते समय पहले मधुर हो जाकर फेनिल हुए कफ को उभारता है।
english: That (food), however, though containing all tastes (rasa), as it is being cooked, first becomes sweet and stirs up Kapha, become foamy.

text_flags.why: possible: 'tas' has no sense here; neuter 'tat' (the food) agrees with pacyamānam

notes: Printed 'tastu' is read as tat tu (the food is the subject; the participles are neuter singular). 'sarvarasa' = having all tastes. udīrayati = stirs up (sets in motion).
lines_deva: तस्तु सर्वरसमपि पच्यमानमादौ मधुरीभूतं कफं फेनीभूतमूदीरयति
lines_iast: tastu sarvarasamapi pacyamānamādau madhurībhūtaṃ kaphaṃ phenībhūtamūdīrayati

hindi: तब जला हुआ, खट्टा हो गया, आमाशय से खिसकता हुआ, स्वच्छ पित्त को।
english: Then, burnt (vidagdha), turned sour, falling away from the āmāśaya, (it stirs up) clear Pitta.
notes: Elliptical: the verb udīrayati (stirs up) is carried from line 109 (card 98) and is not supplied. The subject (the food) is understood; vidagdha = burnt/overcooked, rendered literally. accha = clear.

words.gloss: digested; seat; pakvāśaya (lower seat of the digested, large-bowel region; probable)

hindi: और पक्वाशय यानी सम्भवतः बड़ी आँत के क्षेत्र में पहुँचकर तीखा हो गया, अनिल यानी वात को।
english: And having reached the pakvāśaya (probably the large-bowel region), turned pungent, (it stirs up) the wind (anila, that is Vāta).
notes: Elliptical: the verb udīrayati (stirs up) is carried from line 109 (card 98) and is not supplied. 'anila' = wind, here the humour Vāta in context.

hindi: और तब इस प्रकार आहार के भीगकर नरम हो जाने पर, पाँच, अस्पष्ट शब्द, वायु से अलग-अलग किए हुए, अनुमानित पाठ पर, अपने-अपने अनुसार आहार में स्थित पाँच ही भूत-गुणों को पकाते हैं।
english: And then, the food being thus moistened, five (unclear words), scattered by wind, each according to its own, cook, on a conjectural reading, only the five element-qualities (bhūtaguṇa) lying in the food.

text_flags.why: possible: the locative absolute is 'viklinne āhāre'; the print leaves the vowels unjoined
possible: damaged print; restoration only a guess, not adopted in the translation

notes: Damaged print: 'paṃcātamaka mahābhūtana mayo' are kept unsplit as unclear; a possible restoration is 'pañcātmakāḥ mahābhūtāgnayaḥ' (the five fires of the great elements, which would give the plural subject of 'pacanti'), but this is not adopted. The grammar of 'vyastāni' and the subject of 'pacanti' are therefore uncertain. Printed 'viklinnaāhāre' is read as viklinne āhāre (the vowels are not joined in print). Compare the bhūtāgnis in line 103 (card 93). The neuter plural 'vyastāni' suggests a neuter subject (such as mahābhūtāni) rather than the masculine 'mahābhūtāgnayaḥ'; the restoration is a guess only.
lines_deva: ततश्चैवं विक्लिन्नआहारे पंच पंचातमक महाभूतन मयो वायुना व्यस्तान्यथास्वं पंचैवभूतगुणानाहारस्थान् पचंति
lines_iast: tataścaivaṃ viklinnaāhāre paṃca paṃcātamaka mahābhūtana mayo vāyunā vyastānyathāsvaṃ paṃcaivabhūtaguṇānāhārasthān pacaṃti

hindi: वे पके हुए फिर अपने-अपने अनुसार ही शरीर में स्थित और अपने अविकृत रूप वाले भूत-गुणों को पुष्ट करते हैं।
english: Those, cooked, again, each according to its own, nourish the element-qualities (bhūtaguṇa) that rest in the body and are of their own unaltered nature.
notes: 'svāvikārabhūtān' is read as sva-avikāra-bhūtān ('being of their own unaltered nature'); the alternative sva-vikāra-bhūtān ('being their own modifications') is possible. 'te' = the five element-qualities (understood from 112).
lines_deva: ते पक्काः पुनर्यथास्वमेव देहाश्रितांश्च स्वाविकारभूतान् भूतगुणानाप्याययंति
lines_iast: te pakkāḥ punaryathāsvameva dehāśritāṃśca svāvikārabhūtān bhūtaguṇānāpyāyayaṃti

hindi: और इस प्रकार पके हुए आहार से, मानो अनेक औषधों को भीतर रखने वाले स्नेह से, रस नामक स्वच्छ सार और किट्ट नामक मल उत्पन्न होता है।
english: And thus, from the digested food, as if from an oil having various medicines in its core, a clear essence named rasa and a waste (mala) named kiṭṭa are produced.
notes: The simile 'vividhauṣadhagarbhād iva snehāt' (as if from an oil with various medicinal substances inside) is kept literal; its exact point is not stated. 'pakka' = pakva (kk spelling). 'kiṭṭa' = refuse of food. The verb is singular for two subjects.
lines_deva: एवं च पक्कादाहाराद्विविधौषधगर्भादिव स्नेहादच्छः सारभूतो रसाख्यः किट्टाख्यश्चमलोऽभिनिर्वर्तते
lines_iast: evaṃ ca pakkādāhārādvividhauṣadhagarbhādiva snehādacchaḥ sārabhūto rasākhyaḥ kiṭṭākhyaścamalo'bhinirvartate

words.gram: bahuvrīhi, m. acc. sg. as ind.

hindi: और उन सार और मल दोनों से, उसी स्वरूप वाले, धातु नामक शारीरिक गुणों के स्रोतस् अपने-अपने अनुसार क्रम से अटूट प्रवाह में भरे जाते हैं।
english: And by those two, the essence and the waste, the srotas of the bodily qualities having just that nature, named dhātus, are each filled in succession in an unbroken stream.

text_flags.why: possible: dhātu + ākhyāna gives dhātvākhyāna; the printed 'dhātuv-' has a stray u

notes: Printed 'dhātuvākhyānāṃ' is read as dhātvākhyānām (extra 'u'). 'śārīraguṇa' (bodily qualities) is a loose term for the dhātus here. The sense of 'tadātmaka' (having the nature of those) is plain; the exact relation of 'sāra' to the dhātus is not spelt out.
lines_deva: ताभ्यां च सारमलाभ्यां तदात्मकानामेव शारीरगुणानां धातुवाख्यानां यथास्वं स्रोतांसि पारंपर्येणाव्यवच्छिन्नसंतानमापूर्यंते
lines_iast: tābhyāṃ ca sāramalābhyāṃ tadātmakānāmeva śārīraguṇānāṃ dhātuvākhyānāṃ yathāsvaṃ srotāṃsi pāraṃparyeṇāvyavacchinnasaṃtānamāpūryaṃte

hindi: और स्रोतसों से विभाग के अनुसार, आवश्यकता के अनुसार ही धातु पुष्ट होते हैं।
english: And from the srotas, according to division and according to need, the dhātus are nourished.

text_flags.why: possible: 'yathātham' is not a word; yathārtham (according to need) fits

notes: Printed 'strotobhyaḥ' for srotobhyaḥ (orthographic normalisation recorded in the glossary). 'yathāthameva' is read as yathārtham eva ('according to need'); the r is lost in print.

words.gram: pres. mid. part. ā-√pyāy, n. gen. pl.

hindi: बाद-बाद वाले के प्रवेश करने पर भी, समय पर आहार के ठीक सेवन से परिणाम के साथ पोषित होते हुए पहले वाले स्रोतसों का क्षय नहीं होता।
english: Even with the successive entry of each later one, there is no wasting (apacaya) of the earlier srotas, which are nourished in due time by the proper use of food, with transformation.
notes: Printed 'pariṇāmavatāpyāyamānānāṃ' is read as pariṇāmavat + āpyāyamānānām. 'uttarottarānupraveśa' (each later one entering the earlier) is read loosely as the later stages drawing on the earlier ones; the wording leaves the exact process unstated. Not translated further.
lines_deva: उत्तरोत्तरानुप्रवेशेऽपि च पूर्वेषां स्रोतसां यथाकालं सम्यगाहारोपयोगेन परिणामवताप्यायमानानां नापचयो भवति
lines_iast: uttarottarānupraveśe'pi ca pūrveṣāṃ srotasāṃ yathākālaṃ samyagāhāropayogena pariṇāmavatāpyāyamānānāṃ nāpacayo bhavati

words.gram: avyayībhāva/dvandva, n. acc. sg. as ind.

hindi: और तब धातु नामक प्रसाद यानी निर्मल सार और मल यानी अपशिष्ट अपने-अपने मान यानी माप का ही अनुसरण करते हैं, आयु और शरीर के अनुसार।
english: And then the clear essences (prasāda) and the wastes (mala) called dhātus each follow their own measure, according to age and body.
notes: 'dhātvākhyāḥ prasādamalāḥ' = the clear essences and wastes named dhātus (loose); 'yathāvayaḥśarīram' = according to age and body. Doctrinal terms prasāda and mala kept.
