words.gloss: own; nature, state; loss; immediately after

hindi: वहाँ आहार-रस, व्यान यानी शरीर में फैलने वाली वायु से बिखेरा हुआ, अपने-अपने अनुसार सम होकर — पाठ अनिश्चित —, धातुओं की अग्नियों में क्रम से पकता हुआ, अपने स्वरूप के छूटने के तुरन्त बाद, प्राम्रक्तादि — यह शब्द अस्पष्ट है — धातु नाम वाला, यथासमय अटूट बल-परिमाण वाला होकर, शरीर को पुष्ट करके, धातुओं और धातुओं के मलों को पोषित करता है।
english: There, the food-rasa (āhāra-rasa), scattered by vyāna (a wind), each according to its own, even (reading uncertain), being cooked in order in the dhātu-fires, immediately after the loss of its own state, bearing the dhātu name 'prāmraktādi' (unclear), timely and of unfailing measure of strength, having invigorated the body, nourishes the dhātus and the wastes of the dhātus.

text_flags.why: possible: damaged print; conjectural, not adopted
possible: reading uncertain; samaḥ tu or samastaḥ tu

notes: Damaged print: 'prāmraktādi' is kept unsplit as unclear (a guess: rasa-rakta-ādi, 'rasa, blood and the rest', as the dhātu names), not adopted. 'samastu' is read as samaḥ tu (regular sandhi) with an uncertain sense; the alternative samastaḥ tu ('as a whole, however') would need a lost visarga. vyāna is the pervading wind (doctrinal). The parse of the long participial chain is therefore provisional.
lines_deva: तत्राहाररसो व्यानविक्षिप्तो यथास्वं समस्तु धात्वग्निषु क्रमात्पच्यमानः स्वात्मभावप्रच्युतिसमनंतरमेव प्राम्रक्तादिधातुसंज्ञकः कालवदस्खलितबलप्रमाणो देहमूर्जयित्वा धातून्धातुमलांश्च पुष्णाति
lines_iast: tatrāhāraraso vyānavikṣipto yathāsvaṃ samastu dhātvagniṣu kramātpacyamānaḥ svātmabhāvapracyutisamanaṃtarameva prāmraktādidhātusaṃjñakaḥ kālavadaskhalitabalapramāṇo dehamūrjayitvā dhātūndhātumalāṃśca puṣṇāti

hindi: अब अन्न का किट्ट यानी अपशिष्ट: स्वच्छ मूत्र और घना मल। रस का सार रक्त है; मल कफ और लसीका यानी सम्भवतः ऊतक-द्रव है।
english: Now the refuse of food (anna-kiṭṭa): clear urine (mūtra) and thick dung (śakṛt). Of rasa the essence is blood (rakta); the waste (mala) is Kapha and lasīkā (probably lymph or tissue fluid).
notes: [02.06.120] Copula understood. The two items are read as the two kinds of food-refuse; 'accham' and 'ghanam' qualify mūtra and śakṛt respectively. [02.06.121] Printed 'kafo' = kaphaḥ (f for ph, nukta spelling; print habit, normalised). The meaning of lasīkā as lymph is probable, not certain. Copula understood.
lines_deva: रसस्य सारो रक्तं मलः कफ़ो लसीका च
lines_iast: rasasya sāro raktaṃ malaḥ kafo lasīkā ca

hindi: रक्त का सार मांस है; कण्डराएँ यानी सम्भवतः बड़े टेंडन और सिराएँ भी; मल पित्त है।
english: Of blood the essence is flesh (māṃsa); the tendons (kaṇḍarā, probably large tendons) and the vessels (sirā) too; the waste is Pitta.
notes: Whether kaṇḍarā and sirā are part of the 'essence' or a separate product is not stated; the words are given as printed after the essence and before the waste. Copula understood.
lines_deva: रक्तस्य सारो मांसं कंडराः सिराश्च मलः पित्तं
lines_iast: raktasya sāro māṃsaṃ kaṃḍarāḥ sirāśca malaḥ pittaṃ

words.gloss: ear; eye; nose; mouth; hair; pore; genital organ

hindi: मांस का सार मेद यानी चर्बी, त्वचाएँ और वसा यानी मांस की चर्बी है; किट्ट कान, आँख, नाक, मुख, रोमकूप और जननेन्द्रिय के मल हैं।
english: Of flesh the essence is fat (medas), the skins (tvacaḥ, plural) and vasā (muscle fat); the refuse is the wastes of the ear, eye, nose, mouth, hair-pores and genital organ.
notes: The print leaves a space before 'malāḥ' (karṇākṣi...prajanana malāḥ) though it is one compound; read as one. 'tvacaḥ' taken as nominative plural (layers of skin). 'prajanana' = generative organ. Copula understood.
lines_deva: मांसस्यसारो मेदस्त्वचो वसा च किट्टं कर्णाक्षिनासिकास्यरोमकूपप्रजनन मलाः
lines_iast: māṃsasyasāro medastvaco vasā ca kiṭṭaṃ karṇākṣināsikāsyaromakūpaprajanana malāḥ

words.gloss: hair of the head (keśa); body hair (loman)

hindi: मेद यानी चर्बी का सार अस्थि, स्नायु यानी हड्डियों को बाँधने वाले तन्तु और सन्धियाँ हैं; किट्ट यानी अपशिष्ट पसीना है। अस्थि का सार मज्जा यानी हड्डी के भीतर का गूदा है; किट्ट यानी अपशिष्ट केश, रोम यानी शरीर के बाल और नख हैं।
english: Of fat (medas), the essence (sāra) is bone (asthi), ligaments (snāyu) and joints (sandhi); the waste (kiṭṭa) is sweat. Of bone (asthi), the essence is marrow (majjā); the waste (kiṭṭa) is the hair of the head, the body hair (loman) and the nails.

text_flags.why: words not separated in print; no sandhi applies at the junction (majjā ends in a long vowel, kiṭṭam begins with k); read as two words: essence = marrow, waste = hair etc.

notes: [02.06.124] Copula understood. asthi-snāyu-sandhayaḥ is read as one dvandva list of three items (bone, ligaments, joints), all given as the essence as printed; the alternative 'joints of bone and ligament' is possible. The pattern essence (sāra) / waste (kiṭṭa or mala) for each dhātu continues from lines 121-123 (card 109/111) (chunk 3). [02.06.125] Copula understood. 'majjākiṭṭaṃ' is split into two words because the sense (essence, then waste) requires it and the neighbouring units follow this pattern; a compound 'marrow-waste' does not fit. majjā = marrow in this anatomy unit.

hindi: मज्जा का तो सार शुक्र यानी वीर्य है; मल यानी अपशिष्ट आँख का मल और त्वचाओं का स्नेह यानी तेल या वसा है।
english: Of marrow (majjan), however, the essence is śukra (semen); the waste (mala) is the excrement of the eye (akṣi-viṭ) and the oiliness (sneha) of the skins.
notes: Copula understood. 'tvacām' = of the skins (plural, as elsewhere in this chapter). The two items after mala (eye-excrement, oiliness of the skins) are read as the waste; the Sanskrit has no 'and'. majjan = marrow here (anatomy unit).
lines_deva: मज्ज्ञस्तु सारः शुक्रं मलोऽक्षिविट् त्वचां स्नेहः
lines_iast: majjñastu sāraḥ śukraṃ malo'kṣiviṭ tvacāṃ snehaḥ

hindi: शुक्र यानी वीर्य का सार ओजस् यानी जीवन-सार है।
english: Of śukra (semen), the essence is ojas (vital essence).
notes: Copula understood. 'sāram' is neuter here, whereas the neighbouring units have masculine 'sāraḥ' (sāra takes both genders); read as nominative neuter, or as an accusative with a verb understood; the sense is the same. Not corrected.

words.gram: karmadhāraya + abstract suffix, f. inst. sg.

hindi: और अत्यन्त शुद्धता के कारण इसमें मल यानी अपशिष्ट का अभाव है। दूसरे लोग तो इसी कारण उसका पाक यानी पकना स्वीकार नहीं करते।
english: And through extreme purity there is absence of waste (mala) in this. Others, however, for this very reason do not accept a cooking (pāka) of it.

text_flags.why: words not separated in print; no sandhi applies at the junction between asmin and mala- (n before m is unchanged)
words not separated in print; no sandhi applies at the junction between anye and punar (the following punar ata eva is regular sandhi)

notes: [02.06.128] Copula supplied in the translation ('there is'), as the noun 'abhāva' needs it. 'asmin' (in this) is not tied to a noun in the unit; it is read as the śukra/ojas of line 127 (card 114) and is left as 'this'. [02.06.129] 'tasya' (of it) is left as a plain pronoun; it is read as referring to the essence of śukra (line 127-128 (card 114/115)). Literally icchanti = 'wish, want'; 'accept' is the natural sense. 'ata eva' = ataḥ eva (regular).

hindi: दूसरे लोग तो शुक्र यानी वीर्य के सार को ही गर्भ यानी भ्रूण मानते हैं।
english: Others, however, hold the essence of śukra (semen) to be the garbha (embryo) itself.
notes: Two accusatives with āmananti: the essence of śukra and the garbha, read as 'hold X to be Y'. The alternative 'they declare the garbha, the essence of śukra, itself' gives the same sense. garbha = embryo (standard).

words.gram: dvandva + abstract suffix, f. inst. sg.

words.gloss: slight (īṣat); sound (śabda); abundant (pracura); sense of the compound uncertain

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर: वायु तो अग्नि और आहार की अधिकता और अल्पता से, उस-उस विशेष मूर्च्छना यानी सम्भवतः प्रबलता से, अमूर्त, शब्द वाला, थोड़े शब्द में प्रचुर, अथवा अल्प, पञ्चात्मा यानी पाँच स्वरूप वाला होकर कोष्ठ यानी पेट के भीतरी भाग में प्रकट होता है।
english: On a conjectural reading: Wind (vāyu), however, through the abundance and scarcity of the fire (agni) and of the food, from this-and-that particular mūrcchanā (probably intensification), appears in the koṣṭha (storehouse, belly cavity), non-corporeal (amūrta), sound-possessing, abundant in slight sound, or small, five-natured (pañcātmā).

text_flags.why: possible: 'ātamā' is not a word; pañcātmā ('five-natured', the wind with five forms) fits the sense and differs by one stray letter

words not separated in print; no sandhi applies at the junction between the two tasmāt (t before t is unchanged); the following t+m→n, d+a are regular sandhi. Also amūrttaḥ = amūrtaḥ (rtt normalisation, recorded once in the glossary)
words not separated in print; no sandhi applies at the junction between śabdavān and īṣat- (n after a long vowel before a vowel is unchanged)

notes: Hard sentence; confidence low. (1) 'pañcātmā' is adopted for printed 'paṃcātamā', hence the conjectural mark. (2) mūrcchanā: sense uncertain (swoon / thickening / intensification); kept as mūrcchanā with a hedged gloss. (3) 'īṣacchabdapracuro'lpo vā': read as three descriptors of the wind, 'īṣat-śabda-pracura' (abundant in slight sound; literal) and 'alpa' (small) joined by vā; it may instead mean 'with slight or abundant sound, or small'. (4) bahvalpatayā is a dvandva: 'abundance and scarcity' (literal), natural sense 'according to how much or how little'. (5) The five forms (pañcātmā) are not named here.
lines_deva: वायुः पुनरग्नेराहारस्य च बह्वल्पतया तस्मात्तस्मान्मूर्च्छनाविशेषादमूर्त्तः शब्दवानीषच्छब्दप्रचुरोऽल्पो वा पंचातमा कोष्ठे प्रादुर्भवति
lines_iast: vāyuḥ punaragnerāhārasya ca bahvalpatayā tasmāttasmānmūrcchanāviśeṣādamūrttaḥ śabdavānīṣacchabdapracuro'lpo vā paṃcātamā koṣṭhe prādurbhavati

hindi: और ऐसा करके देह में सभी भाव यानी पदार्थ या अवस्थाएँ अन्न से बने हुए ही हैं।
english: And having thus done, all states (bhāva) in the body are made of food alone.
notes: 'evaṃ kṛtvā' is rendered literally; the idiom is probably 'this being so'. Copula understood. 'annamayā' is annamayāḥ with the visarga lost before eva (regular -āḥ + vowel).
lines_deva: एवं च कृत्वा देहेऽन्नमया एव सर्वे भावाः
lines_iast: evaṃ ca kṛtvā dehe'nnamayā eva sarve bhāvāḥ

hindi: उसी से यह शरीर-यन्त्र इस प्रकार देर तक, भीतर और बाहर न्यास यानी धरोहर के रूप में, अटूट प्रवाह के साथ, स्वास्थ्य, बल और वृद्धि से युक्त होकर, जब तक कर्म का उपादान यानी ग्रहण है तब तक चलाया जाता है।
english: By that alone, this body-machine (śarīra-yantra), thus, for a long time, as a deposit (nyāsa) within and without, with an unbroken flow, endowed with health, strength and growth, is kept going for as long as the taking up (upādāna) of action (karma).

text_flags.why: words not separated in print; no sandhi applies at the junction between antar and bahiḥ (r before b is unchanged)
words not separated in print; no sandhi applies at the junction between yuktam and yāvat, and between yāvat and karma (t before k is unchanged)

notes: Confidence low. 'nyāsam antarbahiḥ' is not clearly construed: nyāsa (deposit, placing) is taken as an adverbial 'as a deposit' and 'within and without' goes with it; other readings (e.g. 'placed within and without') are possible. 'yāvat karmopādānam' is read as 'for as long as the taking up of karma (action)', i.e. as long as karma is taken up; it may mean 'as far as karma takes it'. The subject (this body-machine) is in the nominative/accusative form śarīra-yantram. 'tena' is left as 'by that' (the food of the preceding units).
lines_deva: तेनैव चेदमेवं चिरेण न्यासमंतर्बहिः शरीरयंत्रमनवरतप्रवाहेण स्वास्थ्यबलोपचययुक्तंयावत्कर्मोपादानं याप्यते
lines_iast: tenaiva cedamevaṃ cireṇa nyāsamaṃtarbahiḥ śarīrayaṃtramanavaratapravāheṇa svāsthyabalopacayayuktaṃyāvatkarmopādānaṃ yāpyate

words.gloss: food (anna); rasa; throwing up (utkṣepa); and the like (ādi); bound (baddha); channel (srotas)

hindi: परन्तु अन्यथा, या तो अन्न-रस के उत्क्षेप यानी ऊपर फेंके जाने आदि से बँधे हुए स्रोतस् के कारण, धातुओं के प्रवाह के बीच जो ठीक से जुड़ा हुआ नहीं है, कट जाता है, या रोग का पात्र बन जाता है।
english: But otherwise, either, with the srotas (channels) bound by the throwing up (utkṣepa) of food-rasa and the like, it is cut off in the midst of the flow of the dhātus, which is not duly joined, or it becomes a vessel (bhājana) of disease (vyādhi).
notes: Confidence low. The subject is not stated (the body-machine of line 133 (card 119) is understood; the English 'it' is a bare pronoun for the verb, no noun added). 'vā ... vā' is read as 'either ... or'. 'baddhasrotasā' (instrumental singular) is read with the unstated subject; it may instead be 'srotasāṃ' (genitive plural, 'of the srotas bound by ...'). 'antarā' with the accusative 'pravāham' = 'in the midst of the flow'. utkṣepa = throwing up, ejection.
lines_deva: अन्यथा त्वन्नरसोत्क्षेपादिबद्धस्रोतसा वा यथावदनभिसंधीयमानधातुप्रवाहमंतरा व्यवच्छिद्यते व्याधिभाजनं वा भवति
lines_iast: anyathā tvannarasotkṣepādibaddhasrotasā vā yathāvadanabhisaṃdhīyamānadhātupravāhamaṃtarā vyavacchidyate vyādhibhājanaṃ vā bhavati

hindi: परन्तु दूसरे लोग वर्णन करते हैं।
english: But others describe.
notes: GROUPING: the unit is a lead-in; the description follows in line 136 (card 122) (appears to continue there). The object of 'varṇayanti' is not stated and not supplied.

words.gloss: throat (kaṇṭha); tube (nāḍī; probably the gullet); rush, leap (pluti)
great (mahā); hollow (nimna; probably the abdominal cavity)
licked over, touched (conjecture for printed blīḍhaḥ)
rasa; trace, small portion (leśa) (conjecture for printed rasleśo)
production (abhinirvṛtti) (conjecture for printed abhinirvatti); immediately after (samanantaram)

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर: निगले जाते ही आहार की कण्ठनाड़ी यानी सम्भवतः अन्ननलिका से होकर प्लुति यानी तेज़ बहाव होता है; उसके महानिम्न यानी सम्भवतः उदर-गुहा में उतर जाने पर जो-जो अंश कायाग्नि यानी शरीर की अग्नि से चाटा गया है, वह पाक को पहुँचाया जाता है; उस-उस अंश का ही प्रसाद यानी निर्मल सार नामक रस का लेश, उत्पन्न होने के तुरन्त बाद, सभी धातुओं में समान रूप से, बन्द और खुले से, द्वारों द्वारा, खुले मुख वाले, अकासन्नेषु अस्पष्ट शब्द, स्रोतसों में फैलकर, अधिक भाग पहले जाता है और बारी-बारी से अन्य में भी अनुसरण करता है।
english: On a conjectural reading: Of food, just as it is swallowed, there is the rush (pluti) through the throat-tube (kaṇṭha-nāḍī, probably the gullet); of that, having descended into the great hollow (mahānimna, probably the abdominal cavity), whichever part is licked over by the bodily fire (kāyāgni) is brought to cooking; of each such part alone, a trace of rasa called prasāda (clear essence), immediately upon its production, spread equally into all the dhātus by the enclosed and open (ones), through the doors, into the srotas with open mouths akāsanneṣu (unclear); the greater (part) goes first, and by turns follows in the others also.
